clue.text: Joint that's just over a foot

definitions.text: Joint that's just over a foot

parts.words: Joint that's just over a foot
parts.note: the joint sits literally just above the foot, while the surface hints at a length a little over twelve inches

explanation.surface: A measurement slightly longer than twelve inches, or perhaps a cut of meat of that size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over a foot' reads as a length, but it means positioned above the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically this joint connects the leg to the foot and lies directly above it.

clue.text: A strict or a liberal gentleman?

indicators.note: liberal suggests freedom or loose interpretation, so the letters of the preceding words are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether a refined gentleman is a strict or a liberal sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman is a gentleman in the old sense of a man of high birth.

clue.text: Shrew's tail cut by chap from the French capital, alternatively

indicators.note: cutting the tail removes the final letter of the name

parts.note: Kate is the shrew of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
a chap is a man
du is French for 'from the' or 'of the'

explanation.surface: An oddly specific tale of a small animal losing its tail to a man from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternatively' signals a variant spelling of the Nepalese capital, more often written with TH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an older variant spelling of the capital city of Nepal.

clue.text: The latest possible hour

parts.note: refers to the idiom about acting at the last moment, the hour before twelve

explanation.surface: A deadline description: the very last moment anything can be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically the hour before midnight stands for the last possible moment.

clue.text: Every letter is written in it

definitions.text: Every letter is written in it

parts.words: Every letter is written in it
parts.note: the surface suggests correspondence, but 'letter' means a character of writing

explanation.surface: Sounds like a diary or ledger recording all correspondence sent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like mail; it is a character from A to Z.
explanation.definitionFit: The full set of characters used in writing a language contains every single one of them.

clue.text: Help a character in opera

parts.note: to help is to aid

explanation.surface: An instruction to assist someone appearing in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Ethiopian princess is the title role of his opera, so she is a character in it.

clue.text: Centre right is showing overconfidence

parts.note: a hub is a centre

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the centre-right party is being too sure of itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre right' reads as a political position, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive pride or arrogant self-confidence, especially before a fall, is the Greek-derived term.

clue.text: Possibly shoots ducks with graduate doctor

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O, so two ducks give OO

explanation.surface: A hunter fires at ducks alongside a doctor who has a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' reads as firing a gun, but is a noun: the edible young stems of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Young edible stems of this giant grass are an example of shoots, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Secured — the same numbers of points?

definitions.meaning: fastened with a knot or rope
level in score, as in a drawn match

explanation.surface: Something fastened, or a match ending level on points.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted means fastened, and a drawn game leaves both sides level in score.

clue.text: Fearless, being in flipping saucy papers

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word for saucy is written backwards

parts.note: saucy means pert, cheeky
ID, identification papers

explanation.surface: Someone bold enough to appear in cheeky tabloid newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive qualifying 'saucy'; it turns PERT into TREP.
explanation.definitionFit: Bold and undaunted are synonyms for fearless.

clue.text: Gave credit for writer that's penetrating in the present era

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so the writer goes within the era's letters

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, the present era
a scribe is a writer

explanation.surface: An author is credited for being incisive in today's world.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute something to someone is to credit them with it.

clue.text: Quietly blame Deighton over explosive fallout?

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to take the rap is to take the blame

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the name is written backwards

parts.note: Len Deighton is a British spy novelist

explanation.surface: Someone quietly blames a thriller writer for an explosive falling-out.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragments scattered by an exploding shell are the debris that falls out of a blast.

clue.text: Red Star delivery for dealers

indicators.note: a delivery mixes up how things arrive, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Red Star is a parcel delivery service used by merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Star was a British parcels delivery firm, so the surface is a business transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchants who buy and sell goods are dealers.

clue.text: Contradictory orders to the yachtsman for extra canvas

parts.note: the first of two clashing commands is to remain where you are
the second command to a yachtsman is to set off on the water

explanation.surface: A yachtsman is told both to stay and to go, and adds more sail.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are opposite commands, remain and depart, both given to a yachtsman.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a triangular fore-and-aft sail set on a stay, an additional piece of canvas.

clue.text: The bride will be up in arms over it

definitions.text: The bride will be up in arms over it

parts.words: The bride will be up in arms over it
parts.note: 'up in arms' suggests anger, but the bride is literally carried in the groom's arms across the doorway

explanation.surface: A wedding complaint: the bride will be furious about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in arms' means furious, but here the bride is held aloft as she crosses the doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: By tradition a groom carries his bride across the sill of the doorway of their new home.

clue.text: Canine tenacity?

parts.note: the word for persistence starts with the name of a household pet, so it playfully reads as a quality of hounds

explanation.surface: A dog stubbornly refusing to let go of its bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistence or determination is the meaning; the word's first part suggests a hound.

clue.text: Using coarse expressions, more or less

explanation.surface: Speaking crudely, or giving a rough approximation.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means talking crudely; idiomatically it means approximately.

clue.text: Failed to use a bit over for recycling

indicators.note: recycling remakes material into new forms, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone failed to reuse a leftover scrap for recycling.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsuccessful attempt that comes to nothing is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Unsettled on a flight

explanation.surface: Feeling unsettled while travelling by aeroplane.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means undecided; literally it means airborne, as on a flight.

clue.text: Finish unfinished 'White Stoat' in gallery

indicators.note: in places the shortened animal inside the gallery name

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped from the stoat's name

parts.note: an ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: Wrap up a painting titled 'White Stoat', left unfinished, hanging in a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' looks like a description of the painting, but trims ERMINE to ERMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or bring to a close is synonymous with finishing.

clue.text: Managed to get detectives to reveal rank

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British police detective branch

explanation.surface: A manager got detectives to reveal someone's official rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a position in a hierarchy; it means foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank, as an adjective, means stale and foul-smelling, like spoilt butter.

clue.text: Reformed ladies, they're highly thought of

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women who have changed their ways are now much admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards of perfection are held in high esteem, which is what this plural noun denotes.

clue.text: Rolled and possibly curled around head of hair

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the hair's opening letter
possibly signals another arrangement of the letters of curled
head of means the first letter of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdressing scene: hair rolled up and curled about the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges CURLED to LURCED, and 'around' puts the H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lurches rolls or pitches suddenly, so the two verbs match.

clue.text: Sets firm with unusual angles

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of angles placed in an odd order

explanation.surface: A company sets up shop with an unusual geometric design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets firm' looks like the definition, but 'firm' is the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid that solidifies or thickens is said to set.

clue.text: Cut down meat

definitions.meaning: to fell or hack, as with an axe
a cut of pork or lamb with the bone in

explanation.surface: An instruction to reduce one's consumption of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hack or fell; the noun is a cut of pork or lamb.

clue.text: Animal seen when ocean has left

parts.note: an ocean is a sea

explanation.surface: A creature becomes visible as the tide goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has left' suggests departure, but 'left' is simply L placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine mammal is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Judge of knitted ties and cooked meat

indicators.note: knitted means woven together, so the letters of ties are rearranged
cooked suggests doctored or altered, so the letters of meat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge assessing knitwear and a meat dish, as at a country show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knitted' turns TIES into ESTI and 'cooked' turns MEAT into MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to make an approximate calculation of it.

clue.text: You'll find the answer at the foot of the column

definitions.text: You'll find the answer at the foot of the column

parts.words: You'll find the answer at the foot of the column
parts.note: suggests a newspaper puzzle answer printed at the bottom of a column, but means the base of a pillar

explanation.surface: A newspaper note directing readers to a solution printed at the bottom of a column.
explanation.walkthrough: The column is a pillar, not a newspaper column.
explanation.definitionFit: A base supporting a statue or pillar stands at the bottom of an architectural column.

clue.text: Love going round university for money

indicators.note: going round means the god's name encircles the university letter

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A student's romance going around campus for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' would usually give O; here it is the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency units of the eurozone are money.
